Great — with full physio clearance we’ll return the client to her original 12‑week strength plan but incorporate everything we changed and tested during rehab: the upper-body priority block while hamstring healed, the graded hinge reintroduction, conservative ramp rules, and the conditioning choices we used. The program below is a single coherent 12‑week plan that starts from Week 1 and explicitly shows the adjusted Weeks 3–9 sequence we actually followed (including the protected phase, upper-focused period, and hinge ramp), then transitions back to the original intensification/peaking plan with posterior‑chain emphasis and two conditioning sessions per week.

Assumptions
- Client: 28‑yr‑old female, recreational lifter, full gym access, recovered from Grade I right hamstring strain, physio cleared for full loading as of now.
- Primary goals: increase barbell strength (deadlift priority), maintain upper-body gains made during rehab, preserve conditioning, and avoid re-injury using the conservative hinge-ramp rules we applied.
- Warm-up: 5–10 min light cardio; dynamic mobility focused on hips, thoracic spine and shoulders; specific warm-up sets for each main lift.
- Rest: 2–5 min for main lifts (longer for heavy singles/doubles), 60–90s for accessories.
- Nutrition and recovery: protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day, slight surplus +150–300 kcal/day if gaining strength; creatine 3–5 g/day recommended; sleep 7.5–9 hrs/night.

Overview: 12 weeks divided into 3 phases (4 weeks each)
- Phase 1 Weeks 1–4: Base/Hypertrophy & Technique (includes rehabilitation adjustments from actual timeline).
- Phase 2 Weeks 5–8: Intensification & Posterior Specialization (includes the upper‑focused block and progressive hinge reintroduction we ran).
- Phase 3 Weeks 9–12: Peaking & Maximal Strength (progress to heavy posterior loading and test or peak).

Weekly schedule and general structure
- Frequency: 4 lifting days per week: Upper A, Lower A (posterior emphasis), Upper B, Lower B (squat/secondary deadlift emphasis).
- Conditioning: 2 sessions/week (Cond 1 midweek, Cond 2 weekend). During rehab we used hamstring-sparing conditioning; as we rebuild, include sled/prowler and heavy carries again but progress cautiously.
- Example weekly layout: Mon Upper A, Tue Lower A, Wed Cond 1, Thu Upper B, Fri Lower B, Sat Cond 2, Sun Rest.
- Progression: planned percent targets / RPE ranges for main lifts. Weeks 4 and 8 are deloads. After full clearance we allow heavier posterior loading but keep ramp rules in mind to avoid abrupt jumps.

PHASE 1 — BASE / HYPERTROPHY & TECHNIQUE (WEEKS 1–4)
Goals: build muscle and work capacity, reinforce movement patterning, maintain upper strength and begin posterior building with emphasis on technique.

Week 1
Mon — Upper A
1. Bench press — 4 × 6 @ ~70% (RPE 7)
2. Barbell row (Pendlay or bent-over) — 4 × 8
3. Overhead press — 3 × 8
4. Incline DB press — 3 × 10
5. Lat pulldown or pull-up — 3 × 8–10
6. Face pulls — 3 × 15
7. Core: plank 3 × 45s

Tue — Lower A (deadlift emphasis; conservative)
1. Conventional deadlift — 5 × 5 @ ~70% (RPE 7) — technique focus, conservative loads
2. Romanian deadlift — 3 × 8 (moderate; emphasize form)
3. Barbell hip thrust — 4 × 8–10
4. Bulgarian split squat — 3 × 8 each
5. Hamstring curl (machine) — 3 × 12
6. Farmer carry — 3 × 40–60 m
7. Core: hanging knee raises 3 × 10–12

Wed — Conditioning 1
- 20–30 min steady bike or easy row (if hamstring comfortable); mobility

Thu — Upper B
1. Overhead press — 4 × 6–8
2. Weighted pull-ups / lat pulldown — 4 × 6–8
3. Incline DB bench — 3 × 8–10
4. Seated cable row — 3 × 10
5. Lateral raises — 3 × 12
6. Triceps extension — 3 × 10–12
7. Core: Pallof press 3 × 10 each side

Fri — Lower B (squat + posterior)
1. Back squat — 4 × 6 @ ~70%
2. Front squat or safety-bar — 3 × 6–8
3. Glute bridge / hip thrust — 3 × 8–10
4. Single-leg RDL — 3 × 8 each (control eccentric)
5. Leg curl superset with goblet squats — 3 × 12 / 10
6. Calf raises — 3 × 12–15
7. Core: bird dog 3 × 8 each

Sat — Conditioning 2
- 20–25 min sled or prowler technique (moderate load) or 8–10 rounds 20s/40s intervals; mobility

Sun — Rest

Weeks 2–3
- Progression: increase main-lift weights by 2.5–5% or add 1 rep per set on accessories; keep RPE ≤8.
- Continue technical focus on deadlift hinge and hip drive. Monitor hamstring closely.

Week 4 — Deload
- Reduce main-lift volume ~40% and intensity to ~60% 1RM; accessories reduced ~30%; mobility emphasis.

PHASE 2 — INTENSIFICATION & POSTERIOR SPECIALIZATION (WEEKS 5–8)
Context: This phase includes the real-life upper-priority block during hamstring rehab and the 3-week reintroduction to hip-hinges capped at RPE 6. Now fully cleared, we’ll finish this phase increasing posterior volume and intensity, still using cautious ramp rules.

Week 5
Mon — Upper A (heavy)
1. Bench press — 5 × 5 @ ~75%
2. Weighted chin-ups — 4 × 5–6
3. Barbell row — 4 × 6–8
4. Incline DB press — 3 × 8
5. Face pulls — 3 × 15
6. Core: Pallof 3 × 12 each

Tue — Lower A (heavy posterior day)
1. Deadlift — 6 × 4 @ ~75% (RPE 7–8) — heavier than Base, but controlled
2. RDL — 4 × 6 (eccentric control)
3. Hip thrust — 4 × 6–8
4. Deficit or snatch-grip pulls (technique) — 3 × 5
5. Hamstring curl — 3 × 10–12
6. Core: weighted plank 3 × 45s

Wed — Conditioning 1
- 20–25 min sled pushes/prowler or bike intervals (moderate). Keep sessions short around heavy lower days.

Thu — Upper B (maintain)
1. Overhead press — 5 × 5
2. Heavy T-bar or DB row — 4 × 6
3. Incline bench — 3 × 6–8
4. Lateral/Rear delt superset — 3 × 12/12
5. Triceps heavy accessory — 3 × 8–10
6. Core: farmer carry 3 × 40 m

Fri — Lower B (squat + posterior supplement)
1. Front squat — 4 × 5
2. Sumo or paused deadlift variation — 4 × 4–5
3. Heavy hip thrust — 4 × 6
4. Single-leg hinge or reverse lunge — 3 × 8
5. Glute-ham raise or Nordic (if tolerated) — 3 × 6–8
6. Core: anti-extension 3 × 8–10

Sat — Conditioning 2
- 20–30 min easy bike or active recovery (walk/hike)

Sun — Rest

Weeks 6–7 — (Week 6 continues intensification; Week 7 was the reintroduction weeks during rehab)
Note: Because we paused heavy posterior loading during her hamstring rehab earlier in the timeline, Weeks 6–7 should be adjusted to respect the conservative hinge ramp we used: Week 7 had RPE ≤6 hinge work, Week 8 ramped volume/moderate concentric loads, Week 9 introduced controlled eccentrics and increased volume. Since physio now fully cleared her, we’ll treat Weeks 6–9 as the graduated ramp culminating in heavier loading at Week 9–10. Follow the ramp rules:

- Continue to increase load only if the previous two hinge sessions were pain-free and morning soreness ≤2/10.
- Change one variable per week (sets, reps, or load). Keep initial hinge RPE ≤6, then allow RPE to slowly rise after 2–3 weeks.

Week 8 — Deload (planned)
- Reduce volume/intensity for recovery. Main lifts 3 × 3 @ ~65–70%; accessories lighter. Conditioning short and easy.

PHASE 3 — PEAKING & MAXIMAL STRENGTH (WEEKS 9–12)
Goals: convert accumulated work into 1RM capacity for deadlift, squat, bench, and overhead press while keeping posterior-chain health in mind. The posterior ramp and hinge progression across Weeks 7–9 prepare her for heavier loading. Week 11 is a rehearsal; Week 12 is a test or final heavy week.

Week 9 (return to higher posterior load, still cautious)
Mon — Upper A (maintenance + push)
1. Bench press — 5 × 4 (build heavier)
2. Heavy barbell row — 4 × 4–6
3. Incline DB press — 3 × 6
4. Pull-ups — 3 × 5–6
5. Face pulls — 3 × 15
6. Core: Pallof 3 × 12 each

Tue — Lower A (deadlift heavy day)
1. Deadlift — 5 × 3 @ ~85% (or build to heavy triples if ready) — only proceed if hinge ramp and physio confirm readiness
2. Block pulls (above/below knee depending on weakness) — 3 × 3–5
3. Heavy hip thrust — 3 × 5
4. Romanian deadlift (moderate) — 3 × 6 (monitor posterior soreness)
5. Back extensions — 3 × 10
6. Core: heavy carries 3 × 40 m

Wed — Conditioning 1
- 15–20 min short intervals or sled (moderate) + mobility

Thu — Upper B (speed/volume)
1. Overhead press — 6 × 3 (speed) or 4 × 4 heavy depending on fatigue
2. Bench speed work — 6 × 3 @ 60% explosive
3. Chest-supported row — 3 × 6–8
4. Lateral/rear delt — 3 × 12
